newsitem.title: CANADA: Class action lawsuit filed in Canada over diet drug.
newsitem.headline: Class action lawsuit filed in Canada over diet drug.

text.p: A Canadian lawyer said on Wednesday he had filed a class-action lawsuit against France's Servier SA pharmaceuticals company alleging its fenfluramine diet drug could cause lung disease.
Lawyer David Klein said he believed the case in British Columbia Supreme Court was the first class action concerning the appetite suppressant, sold in Canada as Ponderal.
The drug is also sold in the United States by American Home Products Corp subsidary Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories under the name Pondamin, but the American company is not part of the Canadian suit.
The lawsuit alleges long-term use of the diet drug could cause a potentially fatal lung disease known as primary pulmonary hypertension (PPH).
It accuses Servier of not testing the drug properly and of failing to advise doctors and patients of the risk of contracting the disease.
Officials at Servier's Canadian office in Montreal were not immediately available for comment.
Klein filed the claim on behalf of Joan Matthews, a Canadian woman who took the drug for weight loss and then developed PPH.
Klein said there may be up to three dozen similar patients in Canada.
Diet pills such as fenfluramine and dexfenfluramine, a related drug, have become controversial because of reports they can causelung disorders and neurotoxicity.
